hypotheses: H1 direct covert command:Thiel or a named intermediary privately tasked Vance and Vance implemented the task through an official act.
H2 distributed control:capital, debt, private access, data systems, dark-money intermediaries and aligned personnel constrain Vance without explicit daily orders.
H3 financial leverage:actors controlling Narya payments, note terms, carried interest or portfolio valuations can alter Vance's private financial outcomes.
H4 concealed coordination:common vendors or subvendors transferred polling, modeled audiences, voter-contact data, strategy or expenditure information between the PAC and campaign.
H5 access-gate control:former Rockbridge operatives in the Office of the Vice President manage outside relationships and transmit network priorities.
H6 legal-gap exploitation:financial entanglements influence official acts where the principal criminal conflict statute does not bind the Vice President.
H7 coercive leverage:undisclosed liabilities, compromising information or foreign-linked counterparties created a nonpublic pressure channel.
